articles.title: “My privacy has been violated in more ways..”: How Joe Burrow's $300,000 home burglary put an NFL star's private sanctuary under threat
articles.summary: Joe Burrow’s home burglary became part of a wider investigation into thefts targeting professional athletes, after investigators recovered photographs
articles.body: Joe Burrow’s home burglary became part of a wider investigation into thefts targeting professional athletes, after investigators recovered photographs allegedly showing suspects posing with stolen belongings. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback lost nearly $300,000 worth of valuables in the December 2024 break-in, while the case later drew attention to a broader network accused of handling stolen luxury goods. Burrow also spoke publicly about the invasion of his privacy, offering a glimpse into how the incident affected him beyond the financial loss. Joe Burrow's stolen jewelry appeared in photographs recovered by the FBIBurrow's home in Anderson Township, Ohio, was burglarized on December 9, 2024, while he was in Dallas for the Bengals' Monday Night Football matchup against the Cowboys. Investigators later estimated that nearly $300,000 worth of belongings had been taken, including designer luggage, glasses, wristwatches, jewelry and cash. The break-in left the residence in disarray, and investigators eventually uncovered photographs that allegedly showed some of the stolen items.According to a federal criminal complaint unsealed in February 2025, photographs recovered from a suspect's cellphone showed men posing with jewelry and other belongings allegedly taken from Burrow's residence. Some of the images reportedly featured necklaces bearing his initials and jersey number. Investigators also found photographs of watches, jewelry and cash. Three men were subsequently charged in connection with the case, while a fourth man pictured with the items was not charged in the complaint.The burglary also prompted Burrow to speak about the impact of the incident on his personal life. During a press conference on December 11, 2024, he expressed frustration about how much information surrounding the break-in had become public."I feel like my privacy has been violated in more ways than one, and way more is already out there than I would want out there and that I care to share."Burrow also acknowledged the challenges of being a public figure, explaining that privacy had been difficult to maintain throughout his career. "We live a public life," he said. "One of my least favorite parts of that is the lack of privacy, and that has been difficult for me to deal with my entire career."Joe Burrow's burglary case became part of a wider investigation into athlete homesAuthorities also investigated connections between the burglary and a broader operation involving thefts from high-profile athletes. Investigators believed certain South American theft crews targeted upscale properties and allegedly moved stolen luxury goods through intermediaries. Phone records and surveillance reportedly connected members of the Burrow burglary crew to a New York pawn shop operator accused of dealing in stolen merchandise.The investigation also brought attention to Dimitriy Nezhinskiy and Juan Villar, who prosecutors accused of operating a stolen-goods business involving luxury items. Nezhinskiy later pleaded guilty to conspiracy to receive stolen property in July 2025, according to Associated Press reporting. That case involved a wider alleged operation, rather than proof that the two men personally entered Burrow's residence.In November 2025, the three men charged in the original Burrow burglary were reportedly negotiating possible plea agreements with federal prosecutors. A judge agreed to give both sides additional time to negotiate or prepare for trial, with a hearing scheduled for December 18, 2025, according to court filings reported by ABC News.The investigation also continued to draw attention in 2026, when authorities reported arrests in Argentina involving suspects connected to a broader burglary network accused of targeting professional athletes. However, those developments did not establish that every suspect in the wider investigation had personally participated in the burglary at Burrow's home.In Burrow’s case, the incident was more than the loss of expensive possessions. His public comments made clear that the exposure of private details had been another difficult consequence of a burglary that brought his home and personal life into the spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Ripped by Ex-Packers Teammate in Video After Comments About Steelers HC Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Former Green Bay Packers wide receiver James Jones took issue with comments quarterback Aaron Rodgers made regarding head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Former Green Bay Packers wide receiver James Jones took issue with comments quarterback Aaron Rodgers made regarding head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday.

Discussing the topic on the Speakeasy podcast, Jones gave his thoughts on the situation between his former Packers teammate in Rodgers and former Packers head coach in McCarthy:

Jones noted that the former Packers teammates he spoke to about the situation were backing McCarthy, saying, "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates on there right now. And ain't none of them on 12's [Rodgers'] side."

After the Pittsburgh Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, Rodgers levied some heavy allegations against McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show :

Among other things, Rodgers accused McCarthy of being late to meetings and even sleeping during them, and he also said McCarthy broke down the team with "1-2-3, Packers" instead of "1-2-3 Steelers" at halftime of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Jones played for the Packers from 2007 to 2013 and again in 2015. McCarthy was his head coach for his entire tenure in Green Bay, and Rodgers was his teammate throughout that time as well.

While speaking on Rodgers' comments regarding McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show , Jones expressed his belief that Rodgers' criticism of McCarthy was "weak."

Jones defended McCarthy against allegations of sleeping during meetings by saying that players sleep in meetings at times, and even he himself was guilty of doing it despite his love for football.

Additionally, Jones expressed his belief that Rodgers should have gone to McCarthy with any issues he had rather than airing out the Steelers' proverbial dirty laundry on a public platform.

Jones concluded by addressing Rodgers, saying, "Your career is over. You have played 20-plus years, you're gonna be a first-ballot Hall of Famer. You're walking into the Hall of Fame, you accomplished a lot of things in this league. Coach Mike is still trying to coach. This could end him."

To Jones' point, Rodgers announced prior to the 2026 campaign that it would be his final NFL season before retiring.

Rodgers was looking to potentially make one final run at a Super Bowl, and he had the Steelers off to a great start at 6-2.

Pittsburgh lost each of its past two games and was held under 300 yards of total offense in both losses, though, dropping the Steelers' record to 6-4.

While the Steelers are still firmly in the playoff race and would be a playoff team if the season ended today, they lost their QB1 on Wednesday and will have to lean on Rudolph the rest of the way.

As for Rodgers, it is possible he has played his final NFL snap unless he signs with another team and manages to get in the lineup down the stretch.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce reveals the one thing that makes holiday gatherings with Jason Kelce’s family truly magical
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce is looking forward to spending the holidays with family, even if bringing everyone together takes some effort.
articles.body: Kylie Kelce is looking forward to spending the holidays with family, even if bringing everyone together takes some effort. The podcast host and mother of four says the holidays give her and husband Jason Kelce a chance to reconnect with relatives who live across the country. In an exclusive interview with PEOPLE, Kylie opened up about Thanksgiving preparations, family traditions and why having everyone around the same table means so much to her.Kylie Kelce shares her thanksgiving hosting traditions with Jason Kelce and their familyKylie, 34, is partnering with The Honey Baked Ham Company for its “Traditions That Bring Us Home” holiday campaign, which focuses on how family traditions continue to grow and change over the years. For Kylie, preparing for Thanksgiving means making sure the food is ready while leaving enough room for the unexpected.She explained that her approach to hosting combines planning with a little improvisation. Some things are always on her shopping list, including specific dishes, a turkey and Honey Baked ham, while the rest depends on what the family needs.“I plan for the things that I know I need, things like specific dishes, always a HoneyBaked ham, and then whatever else is going on the table. So obviously Thanksgiving, we will do a turkey. I account for the staples. I plan my grocery trips depending on how fresh I need the items,” Kylie told PEOPLE.She also has a practical way of making the days after Thanksgiving easier. Rather than relying only on the leftover turkey from the main meal, Kylie picks up a turkey breast to prepare sandwiches the following day.“The cheat for Thanksgiving is that you go and you pick up your Honey Baked ham, but you also get a turkey breast so that the next day, when you make sandwiches, it’s easier. You don’t have to keep carving turkey off of the turkey. You can make next-day Thanksgiving sandwiches with the turkey breast,” she shared.Once the main preparations are taken care of, things become less organised, but Kylie doesn’t mind. Her mother often joins her in the kitchen, and sometimes her mother-in-law, Donna Kelce, also lends a hand.“Then, after that, I wing it. It’s like the most chaotic nonsense you’ve ever seen,” she joked, adding that whoever is in the kitchen usually helps make things easier. However, one thing remains non-negotiable for her family.“As long as there’s a HoneyBaked ham - I think my family might get up and leave the table if I didn’t.”Kylie Kelce explains why getting Jason Kelce’s spread-out family together is magicalAlthough the Kelces have their traditions, their Thanksgiving plans may change this year because the Kansas City Chiefs are playing on the holiday. Still, Kylie is looking forward to spending time with the people she loves.She explained that it can be difficult to stay connected when relatives live far apart and everyone has busy schedules. The holidays, however, give families a reason to make time for one another.“We get a little bit lost in the chaos sometimes, of being like, ‘Oh. We should really go see this person,’ or ‘We should really check in or get together with that person.’ And the holidays just, I think, give you that sense of responsibility to be like, ‘No, there is no excuse. We have the time because you set it aside anyway,’ ” she said.Kylie also spoke about how meaningful these gatherings have become, especially since she did not grow up with the same kind of spread-out family situation.“It’s such a beautiful thing to be able to take that moment of pause and get to be around the people that you love. I didn’t grow up in sort of this spread-out family situation that we currently have, so it’s so beautiful when we get to get everyone together. It’s magical, and we really look forward to those moments,” she said.For Kylie and Jason, these gatherings also mean a lot to their four daughters, Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn, who get to spend time with the people they love and build memories together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Not a good teammate”: Aaron Rodgers gets blunt reality check from Steelers owner Art Rooney II after Mike Mccarthy fallout
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers might be used to having the last word, but this time, Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II has something to say.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers might be used to having the last word, but this time, Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II has something to say. The veteran quarterback's recent comments about head coach Mike McCarthy have now drawn a public response from the team's owner, and Rooney isn't exactly pleased with how Rodgers handled the situation.Art Rooney II questions Aaron Rodgers' loyalty to his teammatesThe controversy gained attention after Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and made several pointed remarks about McCarthy. The quarterback reportedly questioned his coach's professionalism, including claims about him arriving late to meetings and even falling asleep during them. His comments quickly became a talking point among Steelers fans, particularly with the relationship between the two figures coming under scrutiny.However, Rooney believes Rodgers should have handled things differently, especially when his teammates were preparing for a game.In an interview with Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reporter Gerry Dulac, Rooney didn't hold back when discussing Rodgers' decision to make his frustrations public."He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure," Rooney said.The Steelers owner appeared particularly frustrated with the timing of Rodgers' comments. Rather than keeping the disagreement within the organization, the quarterback chose to discuss the situation publicly, putting the team and its coaching staff in the spotlight.For Rooney, the issue wasn't simply what Rodgers had to say about McCarthy. It was also when he decided to say it. His response suggested that the comments were an unnecessary distraction for players who were supposed to be focused on football.And while Rodgers may have had his reasons for speaking out, Rooney clearly wasn't impressed with the approach.Steelers owner makes Mike McCarthy's future clearWhile Rooney had some strong words for Rodgers, he was considerably more supportive when the conversation turned to McCarthy.The owner dismissed concerns surrounding the coach's health, saying McCarthy was "as healthy as the rest of us."He also made a strong statement about the coach's future in Pittsburgh."I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney added.That comment is particularly notable because it signals the organization's confidence in McCarthy despite the criticism surrounding his coaching methods.Instead of allowing Rodgers' remarks to create further uncertainty about the coaching situation, Rooney used the opportunity to publicly stand behind McCarthy.Now, with Rooney publicly questioning Rodgers' decision to speak out while backing McCarthy's future, the disagreement has become bigger than a quarterback-coach issue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Steelers owner Art Rooney II says Aaron Rodgers was not a 'good teammate,' expresses confidence in Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Art Rooney II is happy with the way the Steelers responded Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are feeling good about their decision-making following the fallout from Aaron Rodgers' appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. Rodgers was promptly released from the team and head coach Mike McCarthy was retained despite some scandalous accusations from his former quarterback .

While it was overall a pretty awful day for the team, Steelers owner Art Rooney II expressed optimism Thursday, saying he has "100 percent confidence in Mike McCarthy," via an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette .

Rooney also spoke about the decision to release Rodgers, saying the quarterback was not being a "good teammate" when he publicly aired the team's grievances following his benching, per the Post-Gazette.

"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure." Then he added, "In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."

"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."

Then he added, "In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."

Rodgers didn't take that track. Instead, the quarterback ripped his head coach relentlessly during an appearance on McAfee's show. Rodgers claimed McCarthy routinely fell asleep during meetings, led the team in a "1-2-3 Packers" chant and questioned the coach's physical health.

Rooney addressed that final accusation, saying McCarthy is "as healthy as the rest of us." The owner added, "health is not an issue."

Rooney then further continued to express support for McCarthy, saying the coach took criticism for changes Rodgers made during games, particularly in the red zone.

"The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working."

Rooney then confirmed that Rodgers was released after trying to deliver an ultimatum to McCarthy. Rodgers reportedly said he wanted to call offensive plays or be released. McCarthy told Rodgers he doesn't get to make those calls, and decided to bench the veteran with the intention of releasing him in the coming days. Rodgers apparently fast-tracked that release with his interview on Wednesday.

The owner also expressed confidence in now-starter Mason Rudolph, saying the team was "excited and lucky" to have him step into the starting role.

At 6-4, the Steelers are still very much in the playoff hunt in the AFC . And after everything that occurred Wednesday, it might take a playoff appearance to salvage McCarthy's tenure with the franchise.

Rooney may have given the coach a vote of confidence, but Rodgers' words will be tough to ignore if the team continues to struggle on the field.

articles.title: Why does the NFL honor John Madden every Thanksgiving? His legacy lives on through special broadcasts and traditions
articles.summary: The NFL will celebrate Thanksgiving with three games on Thursday, November 26, while remembering one of the biggest names in its history, John Madden.
articles.body: The NFL will celebrate Thanksgiving with three games on Thursday, November 26, while remembering one of the biggest names in its history, John Madden. The 2026 holiday schedule features the Chicago Bears facing the Detroit Lions, the Philadelphia Eagles taking on the Dallas Cowboys, and the Kansas City Chiefs meeting the Buffalo Bills. Along with the action on the field, all three games will include special tributes to Madden, whose work as a coach and broadcaster helped make Thanksgiving football a special part of American sports culture.John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration 2026: Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys Lead the Holiday ScheduleThe NFL has kept its Thanksgiving tradition alive with three games spread across the day. The Chicago Bears will visit the Detroit Lions at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Philadelphia Eagles will then face the Dallas Cowboys at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. The final game will see the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.It remains one of the league's best-known annual traditions.The opening game will be particularly important for Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams. He will face a Detroit side that beat the Bears in their last Thanksgiving meeting in 2024. Williams threw for 256 yards and scored three passing touchdowns in that game, but Chicago still suffered a 23-20 defeat.The later matchup between Philadelphia and Dallas also brings two familiar rivals together. Dallas already defeated the Eagles 38-21 in Week 7 this season. The Chiefs-Bills game will then give Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen another chance to face each other. This will be their 11th meeting as starting quarterbacks, including playoff games.Why the NFL Honors John Madden Every Thanksgiving: His Turkey Leg Tradition and Lasting Impact on FootballThe annual celebration is closely connected to Madden's love for Thanksgiving football. He spent more than 40 years in the NFL as a coach and broadcaster. He won a Super Bowl with the Oakland Raiders and later became one of the most familiar voices in the sport.Madden also became a regular part of Thanksgiving broadcasts. He called 20 games on the holiday during his broadcasting career, working for CBS and FOX. His partnership with commentator Pat Summerall also helped make those broadcasts popular with viewers.One of his best-known Thanksgiving traditions started in 1989. During a game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, Madden gave Eagles defensive end Reggie White a turkey leg for his performance. He continued the idea in later years and made it a fun part of his broadcasts.Madden also helped make the turducken famous. It is a dish made by placing a chicken inside a duck and then putting both inside a turkey. He would explain the unusual meal during broadcasts and even eat it on camera. The tradition became closely linked with his Thanksgiving coverage.Madden died on December 28, 2021, at the age of 85. The NFL started the John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration in 2022 to keep his connection with the holiday alive. The league has continued the event every year since then.This year's celebration will include several special touches. CBS, FOX and NBC will show tributes to Madden during their broadcasts. Each network will also begin its coverage with a special video featuring his own words about Thanksgiving.The NFL will also select one Madden Thanksgiving MVP from each game. Each winner will receive a new trophy shaped like a football turkey leg. The NFL Foundation will also donate $10,000 to a high school or youth football program chosen by the winning player.There will be another reminder of Madden before kickoff. The coin used for each game's toss will feature his image on one side and a six-legged turducken on the other. Players from all six teams will also wear a patch with Madden's image on their jerseys.The league will place special John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration designs around the playing areas at Ford Field, AT&T Stadium and Highmark Stadium. It will also auction game-used items from the three games to raise money for the John Madden Foundation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bears get a huge tackle, last-second touchdown and stun Lions to take over first place in NFC North
articles.summary: The Bears and Lions gave everyone a high-scoring second half on Thanksgiving.
articles.body: Jahmyr Gibbs was running circles around the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. Until T.J. Edwards made one of the biggest tackles of the NFL season. Edwards had to make an open-field tackle on fourth down against Gibbs, who already had well over 200 yards from scrimmage, to keep the Bears' hopes at winning alive. And Edwards brought him down. That gave the Bears offense a shot at the win in the final two minutes. Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze hooked up on a touchdown with three seconds left, on a pretty pass and catch in which Odunze barely kept his feet in bounds for the go-ahead score. The Bears won 39-35 in one of the greatest Thanksgiving games ever. If the Bears end up having a special season — at 9-2 and with a one-game lead in the NFC North, it's on everyone's mind in Chicago — Edwards' tackle and the subsequent touchdown to Odunze will go into franchise lore. Huge tackle by TJ Edwards to stop Gibbs and the Lions on 4th down!CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kWFyGkhRGC— NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Bears trailed most of Thursday's game. Their turnover problems cost them points and gave the Lions some too. Gibbs had a monster game and seemed to put the Bears away with a 70-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. But the Bears, on the road against a team that also entered at 8-2, made enough plays. They're 9-2 now, lead the NFC North, have a big edge in the tiebreaker race over the Lions and their dreams of snapping a Super Bowl championship drought that dates back to 1985 suddenly seem even more real. Offenses start slow in first halfWith two great offenses riding a hot streak, a lot of points were expected to kick off Thanksgiving. That's not what unfolded early on, though. The Lions led 3-0 at the end of the first quarter. The Bears lost a fumble deep in Lions territory when Colston Loveland was hit hard and then had the ball punched out. The Bears had seven turnovers in their previous two games and that problem persisted to start their game against Detroit.The Lions' defense came up with a huge play near the end of the half, with the Bears again being reckless with the ball. Backed up near their own end zone, Caleb Williams was hit in the end zone by Derrick Moore and the ball came out. Bears tackle Darnell Wright batted the loose ball out of the end zone, which is a penalty. The Lions took the penalty and the safety instead of declining it and getting the ball at Chicago's 10-yard line. That gamble paid off when Jared Goff got the team downfield quickly, highlighted by a 39-yard pass to Jameson Williams, and he hit Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown. The Lions led 19-10 at halftime and the Bears' turnovers were a major reason. They had some self-inflicted wounds that were keeping them behind, but they'd still end up doing enough to win. Fireworks in the second halfGibbs had a monster second half. He hadn't scored a touchdown on Thanksgiving in his career but made up for it Thursday. Gibbs led the NFL with 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 total touchdowns coming in and took a big step toward first NFL Offensive Player of the Year award on a big stage. Gibbs rushed for three touchdowns. His 70-yard run down the sideline gave the Lions a 35-24 lead with 8:20 left. Gibbs finished with 252 total yards and three touchdowns, but it didn't end up being enough. Gibbs' big play looked like it would put the game away but the Bears had a comeback in them. Williams hit Odunze for a 41-yard touchdown with 7:20 left to pull the Bears back within one possession. Chicago's offense is capable of hitting a quick score, but it needed the defense to get a stop against a red-hot Lions offense. Edwards made a great tackle on 4th-and-4 from the Bears 33-yard line to give the Bears another shot. Lions coach Dan Campbell loves to go for it on fourth down and sometimes it doesn't work out. The Bears got the ball back with 2:17 to either tie the game with a field goal or go ahead with a touchdown. Williams kept the drive alive with a designed quarterback run to the outside on 4-and-1. The Bears started picking up first downs after that, including one on a facemask penalty that put them in field-goal range. The Bears had nine seconds left and had to go to the end zone on third down, and Williams hit Odunze for the touchdown and a thrilling win. The Bears are 9-2 and feeling good. They looked buried against the Lions on Thanksgiving, but had a comeback that their fans will remember for a long time.

articles.title: From a $680,000 home to a nearly $6 million estate, Jason Kelce's biggest investment is his family's future
articles.summary: For Jason and Kylie Kelce, building a comfortable family life has become more important than finding a bigger house.
articles.body: For Jason and Kylie Kelce, building a comfortable family life has become more important than finding a bigger house. The former Philadelphia Eagles star and his wife have invested millions in neighbouring properties in Haverford, Pennsylvania, with plans to create a larger family estate. Behind the high-profile property decisions is a desire to give their four daughters room to grow while keeping the family rooted in a neighbourhood they already call home.Jason and Kylie Kelce's property plans reflect their growing familyThe Kelces' property journey began with a home purchase, but their plans gradually expanded as opportunities arose nearby. Jason Kelce initially considered moving into a larger house. However, buying adjoining land offered another option: expanding their existing property without leaving the community.Their purchases included a $3.96 million neighbouring property and another parcel reportedly worth $1.35 million. Together with their original home, the acquisitions brought the estimated value of their Pennsylvania estate close to $6 million.The decision also reflects a different stage in their lives. Jason and Kylie are raising four daughters, Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finnley. As the children grow, having enough room for family activities, privacy and everyday routines becomes increasingly important.For a family that attracts public attention, creating a secure environment is another consideration. Their property plans have therefore become about more than adding space or increasing real estate value.Kylie Kelce puts family privacy ahead of public opinionKylie has also addressed criticism surrounding the couple's decision to purchase several neighbouring properties. In October 2026, she responded to questions about their growing estate and raised concerns about people sharing aerial views of their home online.Her comments highlighted an issue that comes with raising children while living in the public eye. Even private family spaces can attract unwanted attention when one parent is a recognisable sports personality.Jason also explained during a zoning board hearing that the family wanted to remain in their existing neighbourhood rather than relocate. That decision offers an important glimpse into their priorities. Instead of starting over somewhere else, they saw an opportunity to create a more suitable home around the life they had already built.The expansion has not been without challenges. Neighbours raised concerns about drainage, construction and the proposed fence, bringing the plans under local scrutiny.Still, the Kelces' broader goal appears rooted in family life rather than luxury alone. For Jason and Kylie, the value of the estate lies not simply in its price tag, but in having a place where their daughters can grow up with a sense of stability, privacy and belonging.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luther Burden III finishes with 44 yards in Week 12
articles.summary: Bears WR Luther Burden III catches three of his seven targets this week and held under 50 yards for fourth time this season
articles.body:
Chicago Bears WR Luther Burden III caught three passes for 44 yards against the against the Detroit Lions in Week 12. He was targeted seven times during the game. He also rushed for one yard on one carry during the game.

Why It Matters: Burden saw a good amount of targets this week but was hot as big of a factor as usual. He has been targeted at least seven times in three of his last four games and should see a similar total in Week 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars . He can be considered a No. 2 receiver in fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs turns in masterful Week 12 performance on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs gave his fantasy managers plenty to be thankful on Turkey Day, totaling 252 total yards and three scores against Chicago.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 205 yards and three touchdowns on 21 carries and caught all five of his targets for 47 more yards in Week 12 against the Chicago Bears .

Why It Matters: As if it wasn't obvious from his totals, Gibbs was sensational. He showcased his power on a 1-yard TD run early in the second quarter, added another 1-yarder midway through the third and raced past the Chicago defense for a 70-yard score in the fourth that should have sealed the deal for the Lions. Either way, Gibbs proved yet again why he will probably be the fantasy MVP. He will be the odds-on favorite to be the overall RB1 in each of the next two weeks as Detroit faces Atlanta and Tennessee.

articles.title: Instant analysis from Bears' impressive comeback win vs. Lions
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears mounted an impressive 39-35 comeback win against the Detroit Lions. It was one of their best wins in the Ben Johnson era.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are one of two NFL teams guaranteed to host a game on Thanksgiving. With the Chicago Bears playing in the same division, they get the honor of being the road team a fair amount of times. It usually is them whenever they have a halfway decent chance of being a good team. Chicago helps TV ratings in these spots, especially if the Bears are playoff-bound.

This was much more than a holiday match, however, as control of the NFC North was on the line. The Bears and Lions, both 8-2 coming in, were one game ahead of the Minnesota Vikings. We already know the result of the Green Bay Packers' matchup, as they lost to the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

Whoever would win this game in Detroit would be 9-2 and have a one-game lead and the early tiebreaker over the other. Having the potential to be the No. 1 seed is one thing, but it's another to lock in playing at home once the playoffs begin.

This game was never going to be easy for Chicago. The Bears haven't trailed since Caleb Williams came back from injury. That changed when the Lions went up 3-0 early. From there, they mostly led for the rest of the game. The Lions are different than every other team that Chicago played during that winning streak. This is a difficult team to play against closely, let alone win.

When the Bears were down and out late in the fourth quarter, it would have been easy to allow the Lions to walk away with a victory. That would have been the result last time they played on Thanksgiving under the previous coaching staff, but things are different now.

In a two-minute drill, Caleb Williams drove the team into field goal range looking to tie the game. However, they ended up scoring a touchdown with three seconds left. They took the lead and shut the door on a rugby-style play that the Lions tried to run with no time left.

This is one of the most incredible wins of the Ben Johnson era. He finally earned a big win over his old team, and it came in a first-place game in comeback fashion. Williams led the offense in a way that only the most elite can at the end of a win under that type of pressure.

The defense had a low-end performance, considering how they've played since Jeffery Simmons arrived, but the offense bailed them out this time. Jared Goff runs one of the best offenses in the NFL, which can be hard for anyone to stop; that doesn't give the Bears an excuse, but it explains a lot. Jahmyr Gibbs ran all over the field against the Bears, but the Bears didn't let it control the outcome of the game.

No matter what, there has been one part of the team that steps up whenever they need it most this season. They certainly have the makings of a Super Bowl contender. Now, they have their Thanksgiving win. We wait to see if they can collect wins on Christmas and Valentines Day.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Takes Aim at Steelers Coach Mike McCarthy Amid Aaron Rodgers Confession on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Kevin Durant, like many NFL fans, wasn’t very happy with how the Pittsburgh Steelers released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on November 25, a day before...
articles.body:
Kevin Durant, like many NFL fans, wasn't very happy with how the Pittsburgh Steelers released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on November 25, a day before Thanksgiving.

Initial reports suggested that Rodgers had a falling out with head coach Mike McCarthy. The QB later went on to criticize McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and the Steelers released him hours later. Later, rumors about McCarthy having an assistant for a very specific task surfaced.

"Happy Thanksgiving, hiring a ice cream sandwich assistant for the day, great idea Mike," Durant wrote in an X post he uploaded Thanksgiving Day.

Durant also showed his support for Rodgers in a separate post by naming him as one of the four NFL players he'd like to have at his table on the holiday.

The report about McCarthy's assistant first blew up soon after Rodgers' benching. The Steelers defensive lineman Breiden Fehoko shared a post on X writing: "Text from a Pittsburgh Steelers player just now 'McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand'"

Fehoko couldn't help but laugh about the report, but it wasn't until NFL insider Jordan Schultz confirmed the rumor that the situation became hilarious. Schultz reported that he spoke with multiple Steelers players about McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant, and "they all confirmed: yes, it's true."

This isn't nearly the first report regarding coach McCarthy's absurd behavior to surface in the past few days. The most shocking claims came from Rodgers himself.

Rodgers was benched in favor of Mason Rudolph. The reasons remained unknown until Rodgers himself appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and listed them one by one.

He told the host McAfee and fans about his disagreements with coach McCarthy on many points. Rodgers revealed that McCarthy didn't want to "get to know" the defense, frustrating defensive players.

When asked to speak with them, McCarthy declined right away, making Rodgers quite upset. This wasn't even the most damning claim made about the Steelers coach.

"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers said. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers even recalled how McCarthy once ended the Steelers' halftime gathering with the words "One, two, three, Packers," naming the team he previously used to coach.

With these instances surfacing one after the other, it's no surprise that Durant openly took a jab at McCarthy. The Houston Rockets veteran has never been shy to voice his opinion online.

Considering that he's one of Rodgers' avid fans during this tough time, it only makes sense for Durant to show his support by expressing frustration towards McCarthy's alleged antics.

The bottom line is Rodgers is no longer with the team. McCarthy remains the Steelers' head coach.

articles.title: Eagles Saquon Barkley, Dallas Goedert injured vs Cowboys. Will they return?
articles.summary: The Eagles lost two key offensive players in Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert against the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas − The Eagles lost two key offensive players within a few plays of each other as running back Saquon Barkley left early in the second quarter and tight end Dallas Goedert left a few plays earlier, late in the first quarter, against the Dallas Cowboys on Nov. 26.

The Eagles announced Goedert's injury as a shoulder injury and they listed him as questionable to return. Barkley's injury was listed as a stinger and he's questionable to return. It's the second time Barkley has suffered a stinger this season.

Goedert went into the locker room to be examined further. Barkley was taken into the medical tent.

The Eagles had already lost defensive back Cooper DeJean to a concussion. Barkley had 5 carries for 7 yards into the early part of the game. Goedert had 1 catch for 9 yards. Veteran Zach Ertz replaced Ertz. It's expected that Will Shipley will replace Barkley if he can't return.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski says Tom Brady ‘told’ him about Aaron Rodgers-esque dispute with former coach
articles.summary: The Aaron Rodgers debacle has divided people across the nation, with some feeling the veteran quarterback was completely out of line with his comments on Mik...
articles.body:
The Aaron Rodgers debacle has divided people across the nation, with some feeling the veteran quarterback was completely out of line with his comments on Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers has now cleared waivers, with the 42-year-old becoming a free agent. Whether a team is willing to take a chance on the controversial QB is another matter. The situation he finds himself in has reminded Rob Gronkowski of some of the situations Tom Brady found himself in.

Although Brady and Bill Belichick won a lot of Super Bowls together, there were a lot of rumours around a frosty relationship between the pair. Gronkowski did not name names, but he did provide insight into some of Brady's private disputes with former coaches.

Rob Gronkowski shares how Aaron Rodgers saga reminds him of Tom Brady disputes

Brady won an awful lot more than Rodgers over the span of his career, with the former New England Patriots quarterback seemingly ruffling feathers behind the scenes with some of his former coaches.

"Being Thanksgiving, this reminds me of the situations that I was in as a player. Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady are the same level of quarterback: they're top-tier quarterbacks in this NFL, both Hall of Famers. I've seen situations personally with my own eyes where Tom and coaches had disagreements," Gronk said on Fox Sports.

"There's one thing that Tom did differently: he would dissect it all, hold it in, and still do what's best for the team, for his teammates, and for the organisation. The disagreements were lethal sometimes. How do I know? Because he trusted in me, and he told me some of them that I would never share with anyone (maybe you guys personally on the low, but no one else in the world). I would see him go out and still be the best player he could be in practice and in games to help win games and win Super Bowls."

The Fox Sports studio did not take well to Rodgers' comments on McCarthy. There was a clear feeling that the quarterback was only acting with his own interests at heart. Some will agree with this, with some feeling that he has spoken out on behalf of players who are unable to.

However, the reaction of the teams around the league will be seen over the coming days and weeks, as Rodgers sits at home as a free agent. Clearly, there will be plenty of concern about the unnecessary distraction signing Rodgers could provide a team at this stage of the season.

articles.title: Wait, Caleb Williams got an X-ray after Bears' epic Thanksgiving win?!
articles.summary: The Bears won the game of the year and Caleb Williams had to... get looked at? What's the deal here?
articles.body:
On Thanksgiving Day, Caleb Williams finished with perhaps the best and most memorable comeback win of his young NFL career. The Chicago Bears superstar quarterback threw two touchdowns, plus a two-point conversion, to stun the Detroit Lions with a late 11-point comeback win to put the Bears on top of the NFC North .

He, uh, also had an X-ray after the game, proving he can truly give happy Bears fans at home both kinds of nerves, good and bad.

According to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune, Williams was one of the last players off the field in Detroit. After celebrating with the rest of the Bears in the locker room, he quietly went off to get an X-ray. Biggs believed the whole situation to be about the Bears using precautionary measures with their star player, but that won't stop people's minds from drawing the worst possible, most pessimistic conclusion until the coast is clear.

That sound you heard when this information was made public was a loud, collective gulp in the throats of Thanksgiving dinner-stuffed Bears fans everywhere. And on a day like this, that had to be super painful:

Fortunately for Williams and the Bears, Biggs' initial gut call was correct. Williams was having his midsection checked out after taking a hard fall, just in case, but the X-ray was clear. Crisis averted. Phewwwwwww:

In hindsight, the fact that Williams was able to finish the game was probably a good sign he was OK, but how could anyone from Chicago think rationally in the moment? They haven't been here before with a great quarterback!

Let a delightful and happy Thanksgiving for football-loving Chicagoans continue as planned.

articles.title: The career-first Caleb Williams accomplished in Bears’ stunning win over Lions
articles.summary: On Thursday afternoon, the Chicago Bears overcame a double-digit deficit to knock off the Detroit Lions in a Thanksgiving Day matchup between the two top tea...
articles.body:
On Thursday afternoon, the Chicago Bears overcame a double-digit deficit to knock off the Detroit Lions in a Thanksgiving Day matchup between the two top teams in the NFC North. Quarterback Caleb Williams came up clutch in a major way in this one, connecting with wide receiver Rome Odunze in the back of the end zone with just three seconds left to secure the win.

The win marked Williams' first win against the Lions in his career, per ESPN on X, formerly Twitter, and put the Bears in first place in the division. It was two years ago on Thanksgiving when Williams suffered arguably the low point of his career during his rookie season, with then-Chicago head coach Matt Eberflus pulling off one of the most puzzling clock management blunders in recent NFL history en route to a frustrating loss.

On the Detroit sidelines for that game was then-offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who is now the head coach of the Bears and has engineered one of the most lethal offensive attacks in the NFL, with Williams leading the charge.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Making the comeback even more impressive was the fact that tight end Colston Loveland went down with an injury that caused him to be carted back into the locker room during the first quarter, and the Bears were still able to put 39 points on the board.

In any case, the Bears will now have a long week off before they next hit the field on December 6 at home vs the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley injury update as Eagles RB leaves game vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Already missing quarterback Jalen Hurts with his blood clot issue, the Eagles have lost RB Saquon Barkley with an injury of his own on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have lost another one of their stars on offense.

Already missing quarterback Jalen Hurts with his blood clot issue, the Eagles have lost running back Saquon Barkley with an injury of his own on Thanksgiving.

Barkley sustained a stinger in the second quarter of Philadelphia's clash with the Cowboys on the national holiday. He has been ruled questionable to return to the Week 12 matchup.

Prior to his injury, Barkley had recorded seven rushing yards on five carries.

Barkley has been ruled questionable to return with a stinger on Thursday, Nov. 26.

The stinger injury was the second that the running back has sustained this season. Barkley previously suffered a stinger on the first play of the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans. He eventually returned to that game in the second half.

Barkley has also missed a couple of games this year with a hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter of a Week 4 game against the Rams.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Undergoes X-Ray After Leading Bears to Dramatic Win Over Lions
articles.summary: Caleb Williams gave the Chicago Bears a Thanksgiving finish they won’t soon forget. After the game, their quarterback underwent an […]
articles.body:
Caleb Williams gave the Chicago Bears a Thanksgiving finish they won't soon forget. After the game, their quarterback underwent an X-ray that briefly gave fans something else to think about.

Williams had imaging done following Chicago's 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune . The reason for the examination was not disclosed, and there was no immediate indication that Williams would miss time.

#Bears QB Caleb Williams just went for an X-ray. He was one of the last players off the field. Was in the locker room for celebration. Could be precautionary. — Brad Biggs (@BradBiggs) November 26, 2026

#Bears QB Caleb Williams just went for an X-ray. He was one of the last players off the field. Was in the locker room for celebration. Could be precautionary.

Brad Biggs (@BradBiggs) November 26, 2026

Williams himself offered a reassuring response after the game, saying he was fine, according to Bleacher Report . He also joined his teammates for the postgame celebration after delivering a performance that moved the Bears into first place in the NFC North.

The X-ray is worth watching, particularly after the punishment Williams absorbed against Detroit. For now, though, the available information points to an examination — not a confirmed diagnosis or a change in his availability.

Williams delivered when the Bears needed him

The third-year quarterback's afternoon was far from comfortable. Detroit pressured Williams throughout the game and sacked him four times, including a strip-sack late in the first half that contributed to a safety.

Williams completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Both scoring passes went to Rome Odunze in the fourth quarter, when Chicago needed them most.

Trailing 35-24 with approximately eight minutes remaining, the Bears cut into the deficit on a 41-yard connection between Williams and Odunze. Williams then ran in the two-point conversion to bring Chicago within three.

The defense gave him another chance when linebacker T.J. Edwards stopped Jahmyr Gibbs short of the marker on fourth down. Williams took over at Chicago's 32-yard line with 2:17 remaining and moved the Bears toward the end zone.

He also converted a fourth-and-1 with his legs to keep the drive alive. With three seconds left, Williams found Odunze in the back right corner of the end zone for a six-yard touchdown, completing a comeback that gave Chicago its only lead of the game.

What comes next for Williams and the Bears

The victory lifted Chicago to 9-2 and gave the Bears their first division win of the season. It was their sixth consecutive victory and put them alone atop the NFC North ahead of the 8-3 Lions.

Williams' health will remain a topic until the team provides more information. He missed time earlier in the season with a hamstring injury, but the reports after Thursday's game did not specify what prompted the X-ray or connect the examination to that earlier issue.

Head coach Ben Johnson said Williams visited the trainers after the game and later had a smile on his face. That aligns with the quarterback's own statement that he was fine, though neither detail establishes what the examination showed.

Chicago does have some extra time before its next game. The Bears are scheduled to host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Dec. 6, giving Williams and the rest of the roster a longer break than usual after the Thanksgiving matchup.

The team is also awaiting more information on tight end Colston Loveland , who was ruled out against Detroit with a left knee injury. With Cole Kmet already out for the season, Loveland's status will be another important story for an offense entering the final stretch of the schedule.

For Williams, the immediate takeaway is that he finished the game and helped deliver a huge division victory. His postgame X-ray is a development to monitor, but his own early assessment gave the Bears reason for reassurance.

articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown surpasses 100-yard mark in Week 12
articles.summary: Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown caught seven of his 10 targets in Week 12 and posted 146 yards
articles.body:
Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown caught seven passes for 146 yards against the Chicago Bears in Week 12. He was targeted 10 times during the game.

Why It Matters: St. Brown recorded his third 100-yard game of the season in Week 12 and has caught at least seven passes in four of his last six games. He should see a similar amount of targets next week against the Atlanta Falcons and will be a No. 1 receiver in all fantasy leagues.
